mechanism_narrative: A CPI level above 320 consistently compresses equity discount rates due to inflationary expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is an always-on signal because the CPI level is continuously observed and the effect is assumed to be constant.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the time periods when CPIAUCSL is above 320.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the time periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% in the past month and FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in the past month, the combined effect of accelerating inflation and monetary tightening compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 1 month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the time periods when both CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In regimes of high housing demand (HOUST > 1300) and strong consumer credit demand (RSAFS > 700000), the S&P 500 produces positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to robust consumer spending and economic growth.
regime_hint: high housing and consumer credit demand
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in less than 60% of the time periods when HOUST > 1300 and RSAFS > 700000.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1300, the S&P 500 produces positive forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to strong housing market activity signaling economic expansion.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 60% of the time periods when HOUST > 1300.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to strong labor market conditions supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 60% of the time periods when UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 105, the S&P 500 produces positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to sustained manufacturing growth and economic expansion.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in less than 60% of the time periods when INDPRO > 105.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI level above 325 indicates persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors demand higher risk premiums.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the time periods when CPIAUCSL > 325.
